chunks: Yūnus, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام

about a child who steals. He said: “He is pardoned once and twice, and he is given taʿzīr on the third time. If he returns, the tips of his fingers are cut. If he returns again, lower than that is cut.”

key_terms.الصَّبِيِّ: a minor child who has not reached full legal maturity
key_terms.قُطِعَتْ: was cut or severed as a legal penalty
key_terms.يُعَزَّرُ: is subjected to discretionary disciplinary punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on a child who steals repeatedly?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a child who commits theft, outlining a graduated sequence of pardon, disciplinary punishment, and then physical penalty upon repeated recurrence. Its significance lies in showing a staged judicial response in the law of theft rather than immediate application of the severest penalty.
